items.title: Show HN: Spewer – Delegate Codex/Claude tasks to cheaper models
items.why_it_matters: A new open-source tool called Spewer lets you automatically delegate expensive Claude and Codex tasks to cheaper models like DeepSeek. Since you want to save on token costs while keeping Claude-level quality, this tool productizes that exact routing workflow. Try cloning the Spewer repo today and routing your next heavy Next.js refactoring task through a cheaper model to slash your API bill.

items.title: Cool little hack using Claude Code watching files with tail -f
items.why_it_matters: A developer shared a hack to keep Claude Code's read cache warm by having it watch a local file using `tail -f`. Because Anthropic's read cache tokens are 90% cheaper than normal tokens, keeping this cache alive across your sub-agents prevents you from losing the cache benefit on new sessions. Try creating a local, untracked `.md` file today, running `tail -f` on it, and instructing your Claude Code instance to watch it to keep your token costs at 0.1x.

items.title: Claude Code can be tricked simply by asking it to summarize a website
items.why_it_matters: Security researchers demonstrated that Claude Code can be tricked into executing unauthorized commands simply by asking it to summarize a malicious website. Since your current project, AI-ingest, is designed to scrape and summarize external AI news, this is a direct security risk for your app's pipeline. Try adding a strict system prompt constraint to your AI-ingest backend today to prevent ingested web text from hijacking your Claude API calls.

items.title: Give Your Coding Agent a Journal
items.why_it_matters: A simple workflow trick suggests giving your coding agent a dedicated `journal.md` file in your repository to track its progress, state, and next steps. This prevents the agent from losing context or repeating mistakes when you start a new session, making your vibe-coding direction much more efficient. Try creating a `journal.md` in your AI-ingest repo today and instruct Claude Code to read and update it at the beginning and end of every session.

items.title: I am no longer letting Claude Code add itself as Co-author in my commits
items.why_it_matters: By default, Claude Code appends a 'Co-authored-by: Claude' metadata line to your Git commits, which can clutter your commit history. Since AI-ingest is your first repository where you are practicing real commit discipline, you might want full ownership of your history. Try running `claude config set commit.coauthor false` in your terminal today to keep your Git log clean and solely under your name.

items.title: AgentObs – a hook that blocks Claude Code before you hit your limit
items.why_it_matters: AgentObs is a new lightweight hook designed to block Claude Code before it accidentally burns through your daily or weekly API budget. If you are vibe coding for hours, it is easy to lose track of token spend until the bill arrives. Try installing AgentObs from GitHub today and setting a $5 daily hard cap on your local Claude Code environment to prevent surprise bills.

items.title: ClaudeDevs: We're permanently raising standard weekly limits in Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has permanently raised the standard weekly usage limits for Claude Code. This means you can run longer sessions and larger code modifications without hitting a wall mid-build. Try pushing through a major feature on your AI-ingest backlog today, knowing you have a much larger safety buffer on your weekly limits.

items.title: Claude Session URL appended to commit messages and PR descriptions by default
items.why_it_matters: A new issue report reveals that Claude Code has been appending session URLs to commit messages and pull request descriptions by default, potentially exposing your private session logs on GitHub. Since you are actively pushing AI-ingest to GitHub, you should verify your privacy. Try checking your recent Git commit history today to ensure no sensitive Claude session links were publicly pushed.
